claim:
Let \(X=(\mathbb R^2,N)\) be the real regular-octagonal Banach plane
\[
N(u,v)=\max\left\{|u|,|v|,\frac{|u|+|v|}{\sqrt2}\right\}.
\]
For the Schäffer nonsquare constant
\[
C_S(X)=\inf_{x,y\in S_X}\max\{N(x+y),N(x-y)\},
\]
one has \(C_S(X)=\sqrt2\). More strongly,
\[
\max\{N(x+y),N(x-y)\}=\sqrt2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
y=\pm Qx,
\]
where \(Q(u,v)=(-v,u)\) is Euclidean quarter-turn rotation. Hence every Schäffer-minimizing pair is automatically isosceles,
\[
N(x+y)=N(x-y)=\sqrt2,
\]
and the Schäffer minimizers coincide exactly with the James-maximizing pairs in this regular-octagonal plane.
integrity: The proof exhausts the full regular-octagon boundary modulo dihedral symmetry. The known scalar value is distinguished from the new complete equality-pair classification. No finite sampling is used as proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is specific to the displayed real regular-octagonal norm and the ordinary Schäffer nonsquare constant. It does not classify Schäffer minimizers for all two-dimensional spaces with minimal James constant.
title: Schäffer rigidity in the regular octagonal Banach plane
